findings.evidence: Engine, 10 ft Rex and Ollie on concrete, all four powers on, hard toss (scratchpad reviewB4/brief/toss.js). At 0% absorbed and a 1e9 kg dial, Ollie leaves at 2,264 m/s with 7.7e9 J (1.8 t TNT). Real air takes almost all of it: he comes back down at 106 m/s. duoFacts counts 1.07e6 J, which is only Rex's hands' air. The same partner thrown straight up on Wrestle > Throw (throwPartner at 90 deg, through MOVES.throw.blast) counts 7.69e9 J and reaches the windows preset. Past 1% of light speed, at a 1e16 kg dial, the toss counts 7.70e16 J at both 0% and 50%; the Wrestle throw counts 3.85e16 J at 50%. At a 1e22 kg dial the toss counts 7.70e22 J at 0%, 50% and 90%; the Wrestle throw counts 7.7e21 J at 90%. On the page (Catch, Ollie as the ball, fastball, 1e16 kg dial), 'Break windows across the street' needs 5.49 million t (a toss at 5,300 m/s, Mach 16) and 'Flatten the houses next door' needs 3.44 million t. Both figures are identical at 0% and at 50% absorbed.
findings.expected: Brief 5a: the blast is 'the energy the air takes in flight ... scales with (1 - share). The courtesy ceiling and the presets judge the boom and blast hazards with that share.' This applies to 'a thrown partner', and the game of catch and a thrown partner get 'the same treatment'. Decision 6 sets the near-field rule: (1 - share) x what real air takes from the same flight, and all of its energy past 1% of light speed. Below 1% of light speed the toss should count k x the real-air flight's drag loss, as the Throw tab and the Wrestle throw do. Above it, (1 - share) x E. At 50% that halves the blast and moves the windows, houses and block presets.
findings.fix: In duoFacts' partner toss, judge the blast with the Throw tab's rule: run P.throwObject(cR, t.obj, 90) at the toss speed (or reuse the toss's own throwObject run t) and take P.RESTRAINT.MOVES.throw.blast(run, mo), which counts k x dragLoss0 below 1% of light speed, (1 - share) x Eobj above it, plus the hand. Do this instead of max(hand, fireball ? KE : 0). Add a powers.js check that the toss's blast at 50% is half the 0% value, both below and above 1% of light speed.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced in the engine and on the page. duoFacts counts the partner toss's blast as max(hand air, fireball ? full KE : 0) (app.html:3844). Below 1% of light speed this leaves out all the drag the air takes from Ollie's flight, though the toss goes straight up and comes back down over them. Past 1% of light speed the share absorbed is never applied. Both break the rule the author set for every other thrown thing: decision 6 is (1 - share) x what real air takes, and all of its energy x (1 - share) past 1% c. Wrestle > Throw at 90 deg follows that rule through MOVES.throw.blast; the toss doesn't. The presets that use f.blast are therefore wrong. On the page, at both 0% and 50%, 'Break windows across the street' needs 5.49 million t and 'Flatten the houses next door' needs 3.44 million t (logKg 16 and logKg 13). By the Throw-tab rule, windows would be reached at about 22,600 t: a Mach 1 toss that real air robs of 1.6e8 J, against the 5.8e6 J that windows across the street need. That is about 240 times less effort. The courtesy ceiling is unaffected, because any supersonic toss already counts as harm ('the toss breaks the sound barrier'). Brief 5a says 'The courtesy ceiling and the presets judge the boom and blast hazards with that share' and applies it to a thrown partner. So the presets are wrong and ignore the slider.

findings.title: Weak-ground exception on a throw: the ground's share comes from the push's own force, but the push is then spread over the 64 ms limb pulse. Lobs in the game of catch and the partner toss skip the cap entirely
findings.location: src/engine.js:1295-1301 (throwObject toGround: Jg = hypot(J cos th, J sin th / sinkRatioRaw), T = max(limbPulse, push.t)); src/engine.js:3219-3226 (throwPushJ: easy throws return the full momentum); tossPartner ~3268 (easy toGroundT)
findings.evidence: sinkRatioRaw is the foot load at the push's mean force over push.t, divided by the bearing. The momentum the ground keeps is then delivered over T = max(limbPulse, push.t), because the code says the push 'reaches the ground through his legs, which spread it over at least a stamp's contact time'. Case: car thrown straight up on concrete at a 1e11 kg dial, defaults. It leaves at 33 km/s and escapes; push.t = 0.15 ms, T = 64 ms. The page says 'The ground takes only the part of the downward push it can bear (0.00047%)'. The engine gives 208 kg m/s, 0.06 mm/s at 5 m, no plaster, and the all-out hazard list has no plaster entry. The bearing-over-the-pulse rule that the jump landing, Collide and growth use, (1.55 MN - his weight) x 64 ms, gives 97,600 kg m/s: 27.8 mm/s at 5 m, plaster out to 8.0 m. Pairing the bearing with the push's own time instead gives 224 kg m/s over 0.15 ms: 134 mm/s, plaster to 6.9 m. Either consistent pairing cracks plaster at 5 m; only the hybrid doesn't. Wrestle > Throw at 90 deg, 2.39% of light speed: 'The ground takes only what it can bear (1 kg m/s); their power supplies the other 22 billion kg m/s ... too little to feel', over 64 ms on concrete that 'gives at 1.55 MN'. The share 1/sinkRatioRaw = RB/(W+F) also ignores his weight: a car straight up on sand at a 1e6 kg dial gives 1,698 kg m/s, against about 460 for (bearing - weight) x 64 ms. Lobs: the game of catch's gentle lob (the default style) of a car at 45 deg and 987 m/s on sand gives toGroundT J = 1.32e6 kg m/s, the full momentum, with no 'supplied'. The Throw tab's same throw (car, 45 deg, 987 m/s, sand) gives J = 9.35e5 with 3.87e5 supplied. The cause is that throwPushJ returns vToMomentum(vL, m) whenever ownAnchor is bolted, and the partner toss's easy style uses throwPushJ.
findings.expected: Brief 5c: the push 'still goes into the ground, so the ground shakes exactly as real physics says', with canon's exception only where the ground couldn't bear it. Decision 22's own principle is 'its bearing beyond his weight over the pulse'. The throw rule, 'its share of the downward push', measures 'couldn't bear' against a force (J/push.t) that the same code says never reaches the ground. The ground should take min(J_down, (RB - W) x T) for the T the shaking uses, as the jump landing, Collide and growth do. The same rule should apply to every thrower's push: full throws, lobs, the catch thrower and the partner toss.
findings.fix: In throwObject, replace J sin th / sinkRatioRaw with min(J sin th, max(0, RB - m g) x T), where RB = qultFor(surface, footB) x 2 footArea and T = max(limbPulse, push.t). Apply the same cap in throwPushJ's easy branch, and so in the catch thrower's lob and tossPartner's easy toGroundT. Do the same for the catch's and the toss's toGroundC with their T. Change the Throw tab's '(X%)' text to the ground's actual take. Add a powers.js check: a vertical escaping throw on concrete has ground J = (RB - W) x T.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. throwObject measures 'couldn't bear' against the foot load at the stroke's mean force (sinkRatioRaw = N(pB/push.t + RB) / bearing). It keeps J_down / sinkRatioRaw, roughly bearing x push.t, and then delivers that over T = max(limbPulse, push.t) = 64 ms. The pairing is inconsistent. For a vertical car throw on concrete at a 1e11 kg dial, the ground is handed 208 kg m/s over 64 ms: a 3.2 kN load on a slab the engine says bears 1.55 MN. Yet the page says 'The ground takes only the part of the downward push it can bear (0.00047%)'. On Wrestle > Throw at 90 deg and 1e16 it says 'The ground takes only what it can bear (1 kg·m/s)'. Over the same 64 ms, concrete bears (1.55 MN - his weight) x 64 ms = 97,600 kg m/s. That is the rule decision 22 itself uses for the jump, Collide and growth. It gives 27.8 mm/s at 5 m, with plaster cracking out to 7 m (not 8). The hybrid also makes the shaking fall as the throw gets harder. The vertical car's ground momentum peaks at 93,500 kg m/s near sinkRatioRaw = 1. It then drops to 65,100 at 1e6 kg, 20,800 at 1e7, 2,080 at 1e9 and 208 at 1e11. Plaster cracks at 5 m only between about 4e5 and 8e5 kg. Harder throws shaking the ground less is physically wrong, and it breaks the monotonic hazard the effort searches assume. Decision 22's 'for a throw or a catch its share of the downward push' is therefore not justified: a share of the force is valid only over the time that force was computed for. The lob part also holds. throwPushJ returns the full momentum whenever ownAnchor is 'bolted', which it always is with They take their own recoil on, so the game of catch's gentle lob skips the cap on sand: J 1.32e6 with no 'supplied'. The Throw tab's same throw (car, 45 deg, 987 m/s, sand) gives J 9.35e5 with 3.87e5 supplied. The partner toss's easy style takes the same path.

findings.title: Weak-ground share for throws, tosses and catches uses the wrong ratio, and the page prints false percentages
findings.location: src/engine.js throwOnce (lines ~1290-1300: over = sinkRatioRaw, Jg = hypot(J cos, J sin / over)); throwPushJ/easyPush (~3218-3226: lob and easy toss return the full momentum); catchLeg toGroundC (~3177-3179); tossPartner toGroundC (~3283-3284); collide held-from-above cap (~2232-2234); src/app.html line 1501 (the 'part of the downward push it can bear (x%)' item)
findings.evidence:
Decision 22 says the ground takes 'its bearing beyond his weight over the pulse', and the jump does that: min(p, (Nmax - m g) x T). Throws and catches instead give the ground 1/sinkRatioRaw of the downward push, where sinkRatioRaw = Nfeet/Nmax. That rule is wrong three ways, and the lob never applies it at all. Sand under Rex bears Nmax = 40.4 kN, and the numbers below are from scratch scripts t3, t6, t16, t18, t19 and page renders p1, p2, p7 and p14.
(1) It counts his standing weight as room for the push. Rex holding the car loads the sand with 42.6 kN before he throws, which is more than it bears. Yet with the four powers on, a straight-up car throw at the 100 t default (all-out) reads: 'The throw drives his feet down with 8.1x what loose sand can carry ... The ground takes only the part of the downward push it can bear (12%)'. The engine charges 5,081 of 41,157 kg m/s to the ground; by the jump's rule the ground can take 0. At 45° the page says 16%, also 0 by that rule.
(2) sinkRatioRaw comes from the stroke's peak force, but the push goes into the ground over the longer limb pulse T = 64 ms. A straight-up baseball at a 10^9 kg dial escapes. The engine gives the ground 0.19 of 2,400 kg m/s (the page's share is 0.0059%), so ppv at 5 m is 0.00 mm/s. The jump's rule gives 702 kg m/s (22%) and 1.34 mm/s, past the 1 mm/s rattle level.
(3) A level car throw on sand reads 'The throw drives his feet down with 1.1x what loose sand can carry ... The ground takes only the part of the downward push it can bear (95%) ... their power supplies the rest'. At 0° there is no downward push, and the engine supplies nothing: J sin 0 = 0 and supplied is 0. The 1.1x is just him holding the car.
(4) The lob and the easy partner toss skip the share entirely. If Rex is bolted or his footing holds, throwPushJ returns vToMomentum(vL, m). Rex tossing Ollie 10 m up on sand (duo Catch, partner, easy style) charges the sand the whole toss: toGroundT J = 42,141 kg m/s, ppv 2.24 mm/s at 5 m, rattle out to 11 m. Rex and Ollie together weigh 59.0 kN, more than the sand's 40.4 kN, so by the jump's rule the sand takes none of it. The catch of that same toss is cut to 4,625 of 42,141 (11%) by the 1/over rule, and the correct figure is 0 too. The page's 'Rattle the windows' preset finds 38% effort from this push alone (the toss is subsonic, so there is no blast).
(5) Collide's from-above cap subtracts only the holder's weight: bear = Nmax - m_Rex g. On sand it credits 702 kg m/s although Rex plus Ollie on top (59 kN) already exceed what the sand bears.
(6) With Unbreakable footing on and own recoil off, the horizontal part (friction mu N, where N is the normal force their power holds up) is charged in full. Car at 45°, 10^6 kg dial, on sand: the horizontal ground impulse is 82,211 kg m/s, while sand can give at most mu Nmax T = 1,505 kg m/s. The push alone reads 157 mm/s at 5 m; capped it would be about 3 mm/s.
findings.expected: Use one rule everywhere, the jump's. The ground's share of a push's downward part is min(J_down, max(0, Nmax - W_static) x T). W_static is everything the ground is already carrying: him, a load held up, or a partner standing on him. T is the same pulse time the shaking uses. With own recoil off, the friction the ground can give is capped at mu x min(N, Nmax) x T. For the car on sand (W_static 42.6 kN > 40.4 kN) the share is 0% at every angle, not 12-95%. For the escaping baseball it is 22%, not 0.006%. The toss's push and catch on sand put nothing into the ground, so no rattle.

On the page, print the share as Jg_down / J_down, only when the throw has a downward part and the share is below 1; drop 'drives his feet down' when the overload is only the static load.

Canon (CLAUDE.md: 'Where the ground couldn't bear the push, their power supplies it') points to the cap, the bearing beyond the weight over the pulse, for the stomp as well. Reproduced. Decision 22 covers this, but its stated reason does not separate the two cases, so the decision is unjustified as it stands. MOVES.jump.shake caps the landing feet's blow at landBear x footPulse with Unbreakable footing on. MOVES.stomp.shake charges the stomp's whole foot blow over the same footPulse, and its real-ground hole time doesn't apply here: 2 x 0.62 / 33.6 = 37 ms < 64 ms.

Decision 22's reason, 'its foot momentum is stopped by the ground either way', is just as true of the jump's feet. So the same event, a foot driven into sand past its bearing, gets real-ground shaking on the Stomp tab and capped shaking on the Jump tab. Canon ('Where the ground couldn't bear the push, their power supplies it') points to the cap. The real ground's large dynamic resistance comes from the sand flowing out of the way, which the power prevents.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced in the engine and on the page. Canon's weak-ground cap (decision 22; README line 105: 'for a throw or a catch, its share of the downward push') is applied in throwOnce, in the catch and in Collide, but not on the gentle-throw path. throwPushJ (src/engine.js 3219-3225) returns vToMomentum(vL, obj.m) whenever easyPush finds the feet hold (e.p null). Straight up, the feet always hold. That path never compares the steady push F0 = RB + mB v^2/(2d) with what the ground bears, and it returns no 'supplied'. So the gentle partner toss (tossPartner 'easy') and the gentle throws in the game of catch (leg/pushT with full=false) hand weak ground their whole momentum, while the all-out throw at the same angle is capped. The hard toss also drops t.toGround.supplied: toGroundT is {J: 833, T} while throwObject's own toGround carries supplied: 679,533.

The effect is not limited to sand. On concrete at 10^7 kg, the gentle 1 km toss cracks plaster to 53.5 m and the faster all-out toss only to 2.3 m.
